## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 (2026)

**My top pick is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**, especially if you want to connect your RV's 30-amp shore-power cord directly to the station.

<row align="start" gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product front view" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="144px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <text weight="medium">BLUETTI AC200L</text>
    <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported discounted price with code AFF5OFF; regular price $899</text>
    <badge color="success">Best for RV hookup</badge>
    <text size="sm">2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery · 2,400W AC output · TT-30 RV outlet</text>
    <text size="xs" color="secondary">Seller: BLUETTI Official US Store. Dealectric reports in-stock availability and a coupon test on Nov. 2, 2026; not independently verified.</text>
    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="View offer and apply coupon"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

The key advantage is the **built-in TT-30 RV outlet**. You can connect a compatible 30A RV shore cord without relying on a standard household-outlet adapter. However, the station's 2,400W inverter limits usable power to about 20A at 120V, not the full 30A (3,600W) of a campground hookup. <Cite ref="turn501845view0"/>

## How it compares

| Model | Reported price | Capacity | AC output | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | **$854.05 with code** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | RV shore-cord connection |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | $899 | 2,074Wh | 2,600W | Output and battery longevity |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $899 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | Lightweight portability |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | $799 with solar panel | 1,920Wh | 2,500W | Budget value |

<caption>Prices are from the supplied search results, primarily checked in October–November 2026, and may change. <Cite ref="turn501845view0"/></caption>

## What can it run in your RV?

With a 2,048Wh battery, expect roughly 1,700–1,850Wh of usable AC energy, depending on inverter losses and operating conditions.

| RV load | Approximate runtime |
|---|---|
| 60W refrigerator average draw | 28–31 hours |
| 100W combined essentials | 17–18.5 hours |
| 500W appliance | 3.4–3.7 hours |
| 1,000W microwave input | 1.7–1.85 hours |

These are illustrative estimates, not measured test results. Rooftop air conditioning is generally not practical for extended use on a 2kWh battery.

**Bottom line:** Choose the BLUETTI AC200L at the reported $854.05 price if your priority is RV compatibility. Choose the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 if carrying weight matters more, or the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 if you prioritize higher AC output and battery cycle life.

The most important question before purchasing: **Does your RV have a 30A shore-power plug, or are you powering individual appliances directly?** That determines whether the AC200L's RV outlet is worth prioritizing.
